summary: Adaptive MI decoding shows a clear positive signal: it achieves the highest HallusionBench aAcc (67.76%, +1.51pp vs vanilla, +0.62pp vs visual replay) while maintaining MMStar accuracy within noise (-0.06pp vs vanilla). The method generalizes strongly to Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct (+3.34pp on 300-item MMStar subset). Criterion 1 is partially met (HallusionBench passes +1.0pp threshold, MMStar does not). Criteria 2 (flip-rate) and 3 (PDM-H) are not yet evaluable pending Tasks 10 and 9 respectively.

hallusionbench.note: Best across all methods including visual replay (67.14)

criterion_2_flip_rate.reason: Flip-rate analysis (Task 10) is pending. Short-budget (128 tokens) vs long-budget (512 tokens) comparison has not been run.

criterion_3_pdm_h.reason: PDM-H vs generation step analysis (Task 9) is pending. No PDM-H trajectory data available.

comparison_with_baselines.vs_focus_prompt: Not directly comparable due to different evaluation pipelines; published Focus Prompt values (51.1%, 55.2%) use VLMEvalKit
comparison_with_baselines.deployment_advantage: MI decoding requires no input modification (unlike visual replay which re-inserts images), only dual forward passes

generality_check.note: Stronger benefit on instruction-tuned model vs thinking model

reason: Verdict is 'good' because: (1) Both main experiment and baselines ran successfully and produced comparable results. (2) There is a clear positive signal -- adaptive MI decoding achieves the best HallusionBench aAcc across all methods (+1.51pp vs vanilla) while keeping MMStar essentially unchanged (-0.06pp). (3) The VD accuracy improvement (+2.37pp) indicates the MI correction genuinely helps the model rely more on visual information. (4) Strong generality signal on Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct (+3.34pp). (5) The method is simpler to deploy than visual replay (no input modification needed). While the strict +1.0pp threshold on MMStar is not met, the net effect is clearly positive, and the remaining criteria (flip-rate, PDM-H) may provide additional supporting evidence once evaluated.
